narrative: In January 2026, UX decisions contributed an estimated $61,000 in cost value, helped ship 14 features on time, and established research coverage across 62% of design decisions — laying the foundation for a strong Q1.

topDecisions.title: Messaging Feature Survey (88% response rate) gave clear direction for improvement priorities
topDecisions.body: 21 of 24 panel members responded to the Messaging Feature Survey — identifying the most challenging features and focusing Q1 improvement efforts where they matter most.
topDecisions.outcome: Clear prioritization signal from 88% of panel membership

topDecisions.title: Feed Advisory Panel surfaced UX gaps before Q1 dev sprint kicked off
topDecisions.body: Panel session with 78 members across 55 banks identified friction points in the new Feed experience ahead of Q1 development. Adjustments were incorporated into design specs before engineering began.
topDecisions.outcome: Issues resolved in design, not in production

narrative: In February 2026, UX decisions contributed an estimated $101,200 in cost value. The Feed Advisory Panel demo drove a 12% increase in new orders in 10 days — confirming that showing clients their feedback incorporated creates measurable business impact.

topDecisions.title: Feed Advisory Panel demo drove 12% increase in new orders in 10 days
topDecisions.body: Director of Product JoAnna Freeland and Director of Dev Joe Myers confirmed new Feed orders are up 12% in 10 days. The increase was attributed to the panel demo — clients seeing their feedback incorporated visibly changed purchasing behavior.
topDecisions.outcome: 12% increase in new Feed orders in 10 days

topDecisions.title: UBA Information Architecture V2 validated — 85.6% task success, up from 67.1%
topDecisions.body: The second round of UBA tree testing (n=10, screened panel) achieved 85.6% overall task success — an 18.5% improvement over V1. 4 participants achieved 100%. Labeling friction dropped significantly, confirming the domain structure was directionally correct.
topDecisions.outcome: +18.5% task success improvement over V1 baseline

narrative: In March 2026, UX decisions contributed an estimated $212,500 in cost value — including a $150,000 POC kill that prevented a misdirected full build. Design sprint lead reached 71%, keeping engineering unblocked across all major product areas.

topDecisions.title: POC killed after validation testing — $150,000 in build cost avoided
topDecisions.body: A product concept in active prototyping failed validation testing against user expectations. UX research surfaced fundamental misalignment between the proposed direction and user mental models. The POC was killed before engineering began, avoiding an estimated $150K build.

topDecisions.title: Sprint lead at 71% — design ahead of engineering across most projects
topDecisions.body: Design ran ahead of engineering in 71% of active projects in March, ensuring dev teams had validated specs before sprint kickoff. This reduced mid-sprint design changes and prevented downstream rework across Feed, Messaging, and Jobs.
topDecisions.outcome: Engineering unblocked — rework risk down quarter-over-quarter

narrative: In April 2026, UX decisions prevented an estimated $76,400 in avoidable spend, helped ship 18 validated features on time, and blocked two product directions that would have required significant rework in engineering.

topDecisions.title: Messaging abandoned a complex filter architecture after UXR showed users couldn't discover it
topDecisions.body: A planned multi-level filter system was killed in week 2 of April after usability testing with 6 participants showed 0% task completion. Engineering had budgeted 3 sprints. UX redirected to a progressive disclosure pattern that tested at 78% success in the same session.

topDecisions.title: Feed design review caught a data display error before dev handoff
topDecisions.body: During a design review of the Task Admin module, a UX designer identified that the proposed table layout would truncate critical account numbers on standard viewport widths. The fix took 2 hours in Figma. The equivalent engineering fix in production was estimated at 3 days.

topDecisions.title: Jobs onboarding flow redesigned based on journey mapping findings
topDecisions.body: A journey mapping session with 4 teller operators surfaced a consistent point of failure in cash balancing flows. The original flow required 7 steps for a task users expected to complete in 2. The redesigned flow reduced steps by 57% and reached stakeholder sign-off in the same sprint.
topDecisions.outcome: Flow complexity reduced 57%; stakeholder sign-off in-sprint
